approved: Defence Amendment (Parliamentary Approval of Overseas Service) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would require approval from both Houses of Parliament before Australian Defence Force personnel are sent overseas for warlike actions.
It would replace section 50C of the Defence Act 1903 with a new section mandating parliamentary approval for such deployments.
The bill includes more detailed provisions for emergency situations when Parliament is not sitting and for information to be provided to the public and Parliament.
Requires parliamentary approval for overseas warlike service by Defence Force members.
Replaces section 50C of the Defence Act 1903.
Adds provisions for emergencies when Parliament is not meeting.
Requires information to be provided to the public and Parliament.
Australian Defence Force personnel and both Houses of the Parliament.

Moved the Defence Amendment (Parliamentary Approval of Overseas Service) Bill 2014 to require parliament, not the executive alone, to approve deploying troops overseas, arguing the 2003 Iraq invasion was a mistake based on false claims about weapons of mass destruction, and noted forty Australian troops died in Afghanistan and two in Iraq.
